questions.q: Why does merging in-store and online sales data happen in silver rather than at gold or at dashboard query time?
options: Doing the reconciliation once in silver avoids pushing that same work into every query that touches sales — transform once, query many times
Gold-layer tables cannot contain data from more than one source
Merging at query time is actually the preferred approach and silver only stores POS data
Silver and gold are the same layer in this project's design
questions.explain: This mirrors Lesson 14's transformation-layer design reasoning: reconcile once upstream, not repeatedly at read time.

questions.q: What is the grain of gold.FactSales, and where was it originally fixed?
options: One row per line item per sale, any channel — fixed during the Project 1 kickoff (Lesson 64), following Lesson 8's grain-first principle
One row per store per day, fixed in this lesson for the first time
One row per customer, fixed in the serving layer lesson
The grain is left undefined until the dashboard is built
questions.explain: Lesson 64 fixed the grain during scoping; this lesson enforces it during the bronze-to-silver conform step and carries it into FactSales.

questions.q: Why does DimStore need SCD Type 2 treatment in this project?
options: Stores change over time (region, category mix), and a dashboard query needs the store attributes as they were at the time of each historical sale, not retroactively overwritten
SCD Type 2 is required for every dimension table regardless of whether it changes
DimStore is a fact table, not a dimension, so it needs history
SCD Type 2 replaces the need for a star schema entirely
questions.explain: This is the same SCD Type 2 pattern Lesson 8 described, applied to a real changing dimension and implemented as a Databricks Lesson 22 MERGE.

questions.q: How is the SCD Type 2 update to DimStore actually implemented?
options: As a targeted MERGE that closes out the old row (setting end_date and is_current = false) and inserts a new current row
By deleting the entire DimStore table and reloading it from scratch on every update
By adding a new column to FactSales for every store attribute change
SCD Type 2 is described conceptually but not actually implemented in code here
questions.explain: The MERGE keys on store_id and is_current = 1, updating the old row's end_date and inserting the new current version — not a full table rewrite.

questions.q: What does Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 27 say silver's role is, and how does this project apply it?
options: Silver holds cleaned, conformed data — here, that means reshaping two differently-structured sources (POS lines and online JSON events) into one unified sales_events table
Silver holds only aggregated, business-ready summary numbers
Silver is optional and this project skips it, going straight from bronze to gold
Silver's role is identical to bronze's — no cleaning happens there
questions.explain: Silver's cleaned-and-conformed definition is exactly what unifies pos_sales and online_orders into one grain before gold ever sees them.
